\[
H = \begin{cases} 1 & D_0 - \frac{W}{2} \le D \le D_0 + \frac{W}{2} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases},\quad D = \sqrt{f_x^2 + f_y^2},\ D_0 = 0.2,\ W = 0.1
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(D\): The distance from the center of the spectrum in cycles per pixel
- \(f_x, f_y\): The frequency along x and y in cycles per pixel
- \(D_0\): The center of the band
- \(W\): The width of the band

D is the distance of a frequency from the center of the spectrum, in cycles per pixel, so the filter does the same thing on any image size. Gonzalez and Woods measure D in samples of the padded spectrum. Divide their value by the padded size to get the one here. The band-pass filter is 1 minus the Ideal band-reject filter. Ringing near edges comes from the impulse response of H, which is wider the sharper the cutoff.
